about: Replaces the single draft integrated-circuit-invented (1959) with two events, at the user's direction (2026-11-06): Kilby's germanium IC (Sep 1958, Texas Instruments) and Noyce's silicon monolithic IC (1959, Fairchild, using Hoerni's planar process). Both come from CSV row 253.

events.name: Kilby Builds the First Integrated Circuit
events.description: Jack Kilby of Texas Instruments demonstrates the first working integrated circuit, built on a single piece of germanium that carries a transistor, resistors and a capacitor. Putting a whole circuit on one chip points the way to the modern microchip, and Kilby later receives the Nobel Prize in Physics for it.
events.note: Split from draft integrated-circuit-invented at the user's direction. Related: noyce-silicon-chip (1959).

events.name: Noyce Invents the Silicon Chip
events.description: Robert Noyce of Fairchild Semiconductor independently invents the monolithic integrated circuit in silicon, using Jean Hoerni's planar process to build and connect all the components within one flat chip. The design can be mass-produced and becomes the basis of virtually every microchip since, powering the computer age.
